item.title: Analytic Properties of Self-Reproducing Families under Contour Convolution
item.description: arXiv:2610.19197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This note grew out of two questions arising in different settings. The first concerns recognizing holomorphic functions among continuous functions on an annulus. The second concerns what self-reproducing subsets can tell us about semigroups of functions arising in analysis. Our analytic starting point is a variation on the classical relation between holomorphy and invariance of contour integrals. It identifies the holomorphic functions as the largest class containing the constant function 1 for which a contour convolution is independent of the chosen curve for every pair of functions. On this class, convolution amounts to multiplying Laurent coefficients. We then study families $B$ satisfying $B\diamond B=B$. We show that expressing a function as a convolution product of $m$ holomorphic functions corresponds precisely to its extension to a wider annulus determined by $m$. This identifies the largest self-reproducing family as the functions extending holomorphically to the punctured plane. We also prove that uniform boundedness on a fixed subannulus surrounding the unit circle forces all members of such a family to have Laurent expansions supported on one common finite set. A general semigroup theorem describes the minimal self-reproducing families.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Ben-Simon

item.title: On generalized embeddability of a non-elliptic self-map
item.description: arXiv:2610.19225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the structure of the centralizer of a non-elliptic holomorphic self-map of the unit disc and its relation with continuous dynamical structures. We prove that if the identity is not isolated in the centralizer of a non-elliptic self-map $\varphi \in \mathrm{Hol}(\mathbb D)$, then $\varphi$ is univalent and its centralizer contains a non-trivial continuous one-parameter semigroup of holomorphic self-maps. This result provides a general criterion for the existence of continuous dynamics arising from discrete iteration. Our approach is based on the theory of holomorphic models and on simultaneous linearization techniques for commuting self-maps. In particular, we exploit recent developments on simultaneous linearization for parabolic self-maps with positive hyperbolic step. As a consequence, we obtain new sufficient conditions for the embeddability of holomorphic self-maps into continuous semigroups.
item.dc:creator: Manuel D. Contreras, Santiago D\'{\i}az-Madrigal, Pavel Gumenyuk

item.title: Eremenko's conjecture on higher-order Briot--Bouquet equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.19243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Briot--Bouquet theorem describes the meromorphic solutions of autonomous first-order algebraic differential equations. We prove Eremenko's conjecture extending it to all orders: if $f$ is meromorphic in $\mathbb{C}$ and $P(f,f^{(n)})=0$ for a nonzero polynomial $P$, then $f$ is rational, elliptic, a rational function of $e^{cz}$ with $c\neq 0$, or satisfies $f^{(n)}=af+b$. In particular, every meromorphic solution with $P$ irreducible of degree at least two belongs to the Weierstrass class. Solutions with poles were classified by Eremenko, Liao and Ng. We settle the remaining entire case with a rigidity theorem for polynomial compositions: if $h$ is nonconstant entire and $D^nR(h)=S(h)$, where $D=d/dz$ and $\deg R=\deg S\ge 2$, then $h(z)=Ae^{bz}+Be^{-bz}+C$. No growth assumption is needed. The proof turns the cancellation of leading terms into a contraction of indicator diagrams and obtains incompatible zero counts near an exposed edge. As an arithmetic application, an algebraic Laurent expansion at one algebraic point and an algebraic value at another force a solution to lie in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}(z)$. Hence any two distinct derivatives of a function in Mahler's class (transcendental meromorphic functions with algebraic Laurent coefficients at every algebraic point) are algebraically independent over $\mathbb{C}$.
item.dc:creator: Diego Marques

item.title: Markov maps and quasi-conformal deformations associated to geometrically finite Kleinian groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.19533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is known that the dynamical properties of Kleinian groups with parabolic elements are much more complex than those without parabolic elements. In this paper, we mainly study the quasi-conformal deformation properties of geometrically finite Kleinian groups with parabolic elements. We show that, for a Kleinian group $G$ with parabolic elements, there exists a subset $K$ of the limit set $\Lambda(G)$ such that the first return map $f_{K}$ is (eventually) expending. Furthermore, the expending property is invariant under quasiconformal deformations. As an application, we show that the geometrically finite Kleinian groups have Ruelle's property. Finally, we use eigenvalue algorithm to calculate the precise Hausdorff dimensions of Hecke groups, which serves as an example to support our results.
item.dc:creator: Shengjin Huo, Wanting Shao

item.title: Weighted composition--differentiation operators on mixed-norm, derivative Hardy and F(p,q,s) spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.19658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study weighted composition--differentiation operators on mixed-norm, derivative Hardy and F(p,q,s) spaces. Explicit dyadic criteria yield boundedness, compactness and two-sided norm and essential-norm estimates, including endpoint and quasi-Banach cases. We also obtain multiplier and approximation results, Schatten criteria on weighted Dirichlet spaces, and exact singular values for monomial weights and linear symbols.
item.dc:creator: Jihua Sun, Junming Liu

item.title: Finite volume quotients of bounded domains with piecewise smooth boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.19807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a bounded pseudoconvex domain with piecewise $C^2$-smooth boundary which has a finite volume quotient for the complete K\"ahler-Einstein metric is biholomorphic to a product of complex unit balls. More generally, the same conclusion holds for a bounded domain possessing a boundary point satisfying Kodama's conditions (C.1)-(C.5), provided the quotient has finite volume for a complete $\operatorname{Aut}(D)$-invariant K\"ahler metric. For piecewise Levi-flat boundary the product is a polydisk and in the smooth pseudoconvex case it is a single ball.
item.dc:creator: Xingsi Pu, Lang Wang

item.title: Entire solutions of higher order Briot-Bouquet equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.20438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a meromorphic function $f$ in the complex plane, we determine when $f$ and $f^{(k)}$ are algebraically dependent. This happens precisely when $f$ belongs to the class $W$ of elliptic functions and their degenerates, or satisfies a linear differential equation $f^{(k)} + af + b = 0$ with constant coefficients. The case of functions having a pole was settled previously. We complete the proof by treating entire solutions.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Eremenko, Tuen Wai Ng, Teng Zhang

item.title: Every Gromov elliptic domain is meromorphically pseudoconvex
item.description: arXiv:2610.20574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every Gromov elliptic domain $\Omega$ in a complex manifold has the following property, which we call meromorphic pseudoconvexity: each boundary point has a neighborhood $V$ such that $\Omega\cap V$ becomes Stein after removing a set which is, locally in $\Omega\cap V$, the union of the polar sets of finitely many meromorphic functions on $\Omega\cap V$. Since meromorphic functions on Hartogs figures extend to their hulls, it follows that, for a domain $\Omega=\operatorname{int}\overline\Omega$ in a Stein manifold, Gromov ellipticity is equivalent to being Oka and Stein, and also to being Oka and admitting a complete K\"ahler metric. This complements a theorem of Matsumura and the author that every weakly pseudoconvex Oka manifold admitting a positive line bundle is elliptic. As applications, we show that the Oka manifolds $\mathbb C^n\setminus\overline{\mathbb B^n}$ and $\mathbb C^n\setminus\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$, are not elliptic, and that no proper domain with Lipschitz boundary in $\mathbb P^n$, $n\geq2$, is elliptic.
item.dc:creator: Yuta Kusakabe

item.title: Mixing Rates for Analytic Observables: Toral Endomorphisms and Anosov Blaschke Deformations
item.description: arXiv:2610.19019v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyze exponential mixing for analytic observables and show that mixing at a double exponential rate occurs for genuinely nonlinear systems. Neither its presence nor its sharp exponent is stable under arbitrarily small area-preserving perturbations in the real-analytic topology. We construct two families of area-preserving Anosov Blaschke product diffeomorphisms that converge in the real-analytic topology to the same hyperbolic toral automorphism. For nonzero parameters, both deformations are topologically conjugate to the linear model but not $C^1$-conjugate. For all nonzero parameter values, the maps in the first family are mixing at a double exponential rate with the same sharp exponent, strictly smaller than that of the linear map. The sharp exponent is therefore not lower semicontinuous at the linear map. In the second family, mixing at a double exponential rate is lost altogether, although the maps remain exponentially mixing. We also establish double exponential bounds for every ergodic toral endomorphism and uniform bounds of the same type for totally ergodic higher-rank toral actions. Our method combines the Fourier escape argument with Koopman operator estimates from a Hilbert space of analytic functions to its dual space of hyperfunctions.
item.dc:creator: Ekaterina Shchetka

item.title: On the Arnold corank, the Zariski multiplicity, and the tangent Milnor fiber problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.19357v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article, we approach the Arnold corank problem posed by Arnold himself in 1975, which asks whether the corank of a holomorphic function is a topological invariant. Here, the corank of a holomorphic function is the corank of its Hessian matrix at 0, which is one of the most basic and fundamental invariants of a holomorphic function. Here, we prove the topological invariance of the corank mod 2. Consequently, we obtain another proof of the Arnold corank problem in dimension 3, which was recently proved by Fernandes, Jelonek, and the author of this article. We also prove that the corank is constant in a continuous family of holomorphic functions with isolated singularities and constant Milnor number. We also approach a conjecture recently posed by Budur, Fern\'andez de Bobadilla, L\^e, and Nguyen (2022), which states that if two germs of holomorphic functions are right topologically equivalent, then the Milnor fibers of their initial forms are homotopy equivalent. We prove that a (much) weaker version of this conjecture, which states that if two holomorphic functions are right topologically equivalent, then the Milnor fibers of their initial forms have the same Euler characteristic, is equivalent to the Zariski multiplicity conjecture for right topological equivalence. Some other results are also presented here. For instance, the multiplicity $> 2$ of generalized semi-Bireskorn-Pham hypersurfaces is an invariant for the right topological equivalence.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Edson Sampaio

item.title: Dimension of the Green measure of skew products with dominant exponent in the fibers
item.description: arXiv:2610.19812v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $f(z,w)=(p(z),q(z,w))$ be a polynomial skew product of $\mathbb{C}^2$ of degree $d\geqslant 2$ and let $\mu$ and $\mu_p$ be the Green measures associated to $f$ and $p$ respectively. Let $\lambda_1 > \lambda_2$ and $\lambda_p$ be the Lyapunov exponents of $(f,\mu)$ and $(p,\mu_p)$ respectively. We show that if $\lambda_2 = \lambda_p$, then $\mu$ is exact dimensional and: \begin{equation*}\dim_H\mu =\frac{\log d}{\lambda_1}+\frac{\log d}{\lambda_2}.\end{equation*} The proof relies on the continuity of the conditional measures obtained by Jonsson, on the fact that $\mu$ has constant Jacobian $d^2$, and on a fibered version of a normal form theorem for the inverse branches of the iterates of $f$.
item.dc:creator: Clara Genes

item.title: Markman--Markushevich principle and Lagrangian fibrations on O'Grady six-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.20044v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: To any compact holomorphically symplectic manifold and a nef BBF-isotropic class we associate a quasi-projective variety called the Markman--Markushevich space which parametrises the Lagrangian fibrations with this isotropic class modulo Tate--Shafarevich twists. We give a systematic interpretation of known results about Tate--Shafarevich twists of Lagrangian fibrations using this space, employ it to obtain a conjectural result for the last deformation type for which such a result is not yet proposed, and make some first steps towards its proof. As a byproduct, we generalise the results of Kumar on existence Shioda--Inose partners for abelian surfaces to a slightly more general class of K3 surfaces, and associate a canonical K3 surface with transcendental lattice isometric to $U^2\oplus\langle-2\rangle^2$ to a smooth cubic surface with a choice of a Schl\"afli double-six. We also review some other approaches towards the construction of complete families of O'Grady six-manifolds with Lagrangian fibrations, and show how they may still be useful even though they do not quite work.
item.dc:creator: Rodion D\'eev

item.title: Von Neumann Type Inequalities for NC Operator Balls
item.description: arXiv:2610.20355v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish finite-dimensional von Neumann type inequalities for commuting matrix tuples in noncommutative operator balls. Let $\Omega=\mathbb{D}_Q$ be the NC operator ball of a linear pencil $Q$ with linearly independent coefficients. If $\Omega(1)$ admits a transitive subgroup of automorphisms with NC lifts and $\Omega(1)$ has the bounded $H^\infty$-Gleason property at the origin, then $\|f(T)\|\leq C_{\Omega,n}\|f\|_{H^\infty(\Omega(1))}$ for every commuting tuple $T\in\Omega(n)$, with $C_{\Omega,n}=(2\rho_{\Omega}K_{\Omega})^{n-1}$; here $K_{\Omega}$ is the Gleason constant and $\rho_{\Omega}$ is the sum of the suprema of the coordinate functions on $\Omega(1)$. The scalar coordinate bounds persist at every matrix level. The hypotheses hold for products of row and column balls, where $\rho_{\Omega}=d$, yielding an unconditional estimate $(2dK_{\Omega})^{n-1}$. For a general type I Cartan domain $R_{p,q}$, we obtain only a conditional result: the same bound holds provided the scalar domain has the bounded $H^\infty$-Gleason property at the origin, which we do not establish when $\min(p,q)\geq 2$.
item.dc:creator: Ran Kiri

item.title: GCD and ABC inequalities for abelian varieties over function fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.20379v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove two height inequalities for rational points on abelian varieties over function fields of characteristic 0. The first is the GCD inequality, which shows that the height with respect to a closed subscheme of an abelian variety of codimension at least 2 is much smaller than the usual height function. This can be viewed as a compact and geometric analogue of a theorem of Levin. The second is a special case of the (geometric) abc conjecture proposed by Vojta, which compares the truncated counting function and the usual counting function. This is a compact analogue of a theorem of Guo, Nguyen, Sun and Wang, and also resolves a conjecture of Buium, which was only known for traceless abelian varieties or constant abelian varieties previously. The proofs of these inequalities follow a common three-step pattern: from microscopic local estimates to local estimates, and then to global estimates. Building on the canonical Xie-Yuan heights, we control discrete counting functions by continuous integrals of Betti forms. The main new tools are uniform Nevanlinna-type estimates for families of linear entire curves on abelian varieties; combined with covering arguments based on Besicovitch theory and averaging, these handle overlaps and gaps precisely.
item.dc:creator: Guoquan Gao

item.title: Deformations of Holomorphic $p$-Contact Structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.20430v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the notion of holomorphic $p$-contact structure, that we introduced recently in the scalar case with H. Kasuya and L. Ugarte and in the line-bundle case with K. Broder, in the context of a holomorphic family of compact complex manifolds equipped with a holomorphic family of holomorphic line bundles. Firstly, we show that the existence of a holomorphic $p$-contact structure is {\bf deformation-open} when a non-jumping assumption is made on the $\bar\partial$-cohomology of bidegree $(p,\,0)$. This ought to become a source of further examples of holomorphic $p$-contact manifolds. Secondly, we obtain a Berndtsson-type {\bf (semi-)positivity} result for the holomorphic vector bundle over the base induced, as a direct image, by the line bundle on the total space that supports the p-contact structures. Thirdly, we introduce a moduli space of relative holomorphic p-contact structures and we show that it is {\bf Hausdorff} and {\bf open} in a certain quotient topological space.
item.dc:creator: Dan Popovici

item.title: On Point Separation of Bergman Space on Stein Manifolds with Constant Holomorphic Sectional Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2602.06813v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the Bergman space of a Stein manifold separates points whenever its Bergman metric is well defined and has non-positive constant holomorphic sectional curvature. We construct examples of Stein manifolds whose Bergman metric is well defined and has positive constant holomorphic sectional curvature, while their Bergman spaces do not separate points. We also construct examples of Stein manifolds whose Bergman metric is well defined and has constant scalar curvature, which can be negative, zero, or positive, yet whose Bergman spaces do not separate points. Combined with previously established results in [HuLi1], this shows that a Stein manifold cannot admit a well-defined flat Bergman metric, and that it admits a well-defined Bergman metric with negative constant holomorphic sectional curvature if and only if it is biholomorphic to the unit ball of the same dimension, possibly with a pluripolar set removed. Our proof is based on H\"ormander's $L^2$ estimates for $\overline\partial$- equations; the curvature condition, together with Calabi's rigidity and extension theorems, is used to construct the required bounded strictly plurisubharmonic functions. The construction of Stein manifolds with positive constant holomorphic sectional curvature for their Bergman metric is based on classical hyperelliptic Riemann surface theory and its higher-dimensional generalizations.
item.dc:creator: Xiaojun Huang, Song-Ying Li

item.title: The Corona Problem for Slice Holomorphic Functions via the Matrix Corona Problem
item.description: arXiv:2608.12258v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we prove the Corona theorem for slice hyperholomorphic functions in a general way that applies to functions with values in a Clifford algebra $\mathbb R_n$ for any $n\geq 2$. This general proof is based on a matrix version of Corona's theorem and then exploiting some symmetries of the matrices that allow to reconstruct the values of the functions. The crucial idea is to tie together the algebra of the functions, the Bezout identities and the Carleson-type conditions. The results we obtain rest on a new way of writing the slice product which improves the standard approach and which holds in general dimension.
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Colombo, Elodie Pozzi, Irene Sabadini, Brett D. Wick

item.title: Transverse analytic envelopes and integrability
item.description: arXiv:2609.05197v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We associate normal toric transverse analytic envelopes with the singular orbits of diagonal holomorphic actions, and construct their canonical flat transport. At independent singular supports, the semiglobal first-integral algebra is determined by periodic resonances; complete integrability is equivalent to full resonance rank and finite envelope monodromy. We classify labelled residual actions with a fixed envelope by Grassmannian families and reconstruct the ambient weights from the labelled quotient and logarithmic residues at full resonance rank. For commuting vector fields in convergent simultaneous semisimple normal form, we identify the algebra of holomorphic first integrals with the common kernel of the derivations induced on the toric envelope. Under compatible flat transport this yields a semiglobal criterion. Polynomial examples show that losses of first integrals may be invisible to any prescribed finite jet.
item.dc:creator: Maur\'icio Corr\^ea, Jos\'e Seade

item.title: Optimal Linear Dependence on Boundary Type for Local Gromov Hyperbolicity of the Kobayashi Metric
item.description: arXiv:2609.15336v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Gromov hyperbolicity constant of a metric space \((X,d)\) is the infimum of all \(\delta\ge0\) such that \((X,d)\) is \(\delta\)-hyperbolic. For a Kobayashi hyperbolic domain \(\Omega\subset\C^n\) and a boundary point \(p\in\partial\Omega\), let \(\delta_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega,p)\) denote the local Gromov hyperbolicity constant obtained by restricting the points to arbitrarily small Euclidean neighborhoods of \(p\), while distances are still measured by the ambient Kobayashi distance \(K_\Omega\). For each even integer \(M\ge2\), let \(\mathfrak H(M)\) be the supremum of these constants over all complex dimensions \(n\ge2\) and all domains whose boundary is smooth and convex near the distinguished point and has D'Angelo type at most \(M\) at that point. We prove \[ \frac{\log 2}{2} M \le \mathfrak H(M) < 36M. \] Thus the optimal universal dependence of the local Gromov hyperbolicity constant on boundary type is linear. We also show that no analogous bound holds for the global Gromov hyperbolicity constant, even among smooth bounded strongly convex domains.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Lou, Jianyong Qiao, Hongyu Wang, yumin Zhong

item.title: Radius of Ma-Minda Starlikeness and Convexity for Functions with Bounded Second Derivative
item.description: arXiv:2610.07845v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A normalized analytic function $f(z)=z+\sum_{k=n+1}^{\infty}a_kz^k$ defined on the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ is called Ma--Minda starlike or Ma--Minda convex if $zf'(z)/f(z)$ or $1+zf''(z)/f'(z)$, respectively, is subordinate to a Ma--Minda function $\varphi$. In this paper, we investigate the radii of Ma--Minda starlikeness and convexity for functions satisfying $|f''(z)|<M$ in $\mathbb{D}$. We first develop a unified approach for determining these radii and then apply it to obtain explicit radius estimates for several important choices of the Ma--Minda function~$\varphi$.
item.dc:creator: Poomalai Palanisamy, Ravichandran Vaithiyanathan

item.title: The sharp constant in the Chang--Marshall inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.15378v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the optimal constant in the Chang--Marshall inequality is $e$, as conjectured by Andreev and Matheson. More precisely, if $f$ is analytic in the unit disk, vanishes to order $m\geq1$ at the origin, and has normalized Dirichlet integral $d\leq1$, then the boundary mean of $e^{|f|^2}$ is at most $e^{d/m}$. Equality holds precisely for monomials. The proof uses an auxiliary closed planar curve and the isoperimetric inequality to establish monotonicity of the exponential functional along normalized radial dilations.
item.dc:creator: Rupert L. Frank, Paata Ivanisvili

item.title: Complex deformations of the circle: Group cohomology and Virasoro uniformization
item.description: arXiv:2605.20175v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We approach the question of complexification of the diffeomorphism group of the circle by considering real-analytic maps from the circle into the punctured complex plane with winding number +1. Such complex deformations form an infinite-dimensional manifold with partially defined inversion and composition operations, smooth in the sense of Fr\"olicher structures, and with Lie algebra relations at the identity given by the Witt algebra. We compute their second group cohomology with real coefficients. It is generated by two cocycles: One cocycle extending the Bott-Thurston cocycle related to the Gelf'and-Fuks cocycle of the Virasoro algebra, and another Euler class cocycle combining mean rotation and conformal radius. Complex deformations act naturally on the (infinite-dimensional) Segal moduli spaces of Riemann surfaces with enumerated and analytically parametrized boundary components, equipping them with smooth Fr{\"o}licher structures. We prove a Virasoro uniformization theorem: The tangent spaces of the Segal moduli spaces are spanned by vector fields induced by the Witt algebra. Finally, we relate the actions of complex deformations to Fenchel-Nielsen coordinates and Schiffer variation on finite-dimensional moduli spaces of bordered hyperbolic surfaces with one marked point on each boundary component.
item.dc:creator: Sid Maibach, Eveliina Peltola

item.title: The Miyaoka-Yau inequality and the delta invariant for Fano varieties I -klt Fano case-
item.description: arXiv:2607.25181v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish the following Miyaoka-Yau inequality for any $n$-dimensional klt Fano variety $X$, possibly K-unstable, in terms of its delta invariant: \[\left(2(n+1)\widehat{c}_2(X)-n c_1(X)^2\right)\cdot c_1(X)^{n-2} \ge -n \left(1-\min\{1,\delta(X)\}\right)^2 \cdot c_1(X)^n.\] Moreover, if equality holds in this inequality, then there exist a finite quasi-\'etale cover $\widehat{X} \to X$ and a positive integer $p$ such that $\widehat{X} \cong \mathbb{P}(1,\ldots, 1, p)$. We also discuss the relationship between Donaldson's conjecture and the Miyaoka-Yau inequality.
item.dc:creator: Tomoyuki Hisamoto, Masataka Iwai

item.title: Regularization and H\"older continuity for complex Hessian equations on Hermitian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2608.15552v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $(M,\omega)$ be a compact Hermitian manifold, and let $\Gamma$ be a symmetric convex cone. We develop a quantitative regularization method for $\Gamma$-admissible functions. As an application, we prove H\"older continuity for every pluripotential solution of complex $m$-Hessian equations whose right-hand sides belong to $L^p$, for $p>\frac{n}{m}$. These results extend to a more general class of complex Hessian equations satisfying the structural condition used by Guo--Phong--Tong.
item.dc:creator: Yulun Xu

item.title: Universality of the conformal anomaly
item.description: arXiv:2608.23201v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The sewing operation is the fundamental algebraic structure of the (infinite-dimensional) Segal moduli spaces as the conformal cobordism category. We prove a universal property of local $\mathbb{R}_+$-extensions of the sewing operation, characterizing them by one real parameter: their central charge. Our result is an analogue of ``Mumford's theorem,'' that appeared in Segal's monograph [Seg88, Seg04], classifying complex extensions, also known as one-dimensional modular functors. Algebraically, the real extensions are characterized by real-valued cocycles on pairs of surfaces under sewing. We identify the disk-disk cocycle as the universal Liouville action, also known as loop Loewner energy. The real determinant line bundle encodes the trace anomaly of euclidean two-dimensional conformal field theories (CFT) and the restriction function of Schramm-Loewner evolution (SLE) loop measures. It serves as the guiding example in our setup and proof strategy, providing the universal $\mathbb{R}_+$-extension. Our results thus give a mathematical explanation for the appearance of the central charge in CFT and SLE, and prove the conjectured uniqueness of Brownian loop measures as the canonical restriction function for SLE.
item.dc:creator: Sid Maibach, Eveliina Peltola
